attention1.ptxt: If you suck at the nipple on the EVAP canister purge valve, you will inhale harmful fuel vapor that may be present inside the EVAP canister purge valve.
Never suck the nipple on the EVAP canister purge valve.

attention4.ptxt: If excessive negative pressure is applied, the EVAP canister purge valve may be damaged.
Do not exceed negative pressure of –66 kPa (–0.7 kgf/cm2, –9.57 psi, –0.66 bar).

s1.ptxt: Prepare to operate EVAP canister purge valve as follows.

item.ptxt: Connect SUZUKI scan tool to DLC (1) with ignition “OFF”.
With ignition “ON”, clear DTC and select “Active Test” mode on SUZUKI scan tool.

attention3.ptxt: EVAP canister purge valve is operated using scan tool as follows.

item.ptxt: EVAP canister purge valve is OFF: 0%
EVAP canister purge valve is ON: 100%
Connect service wire (2) between EVAP canister purge valve (1) and EVAP canister purge valve connector with ignition “OFF”.

attention3.ptxt: EVAP canister purge valve is operated using service wire as follows.

item.ptxt: EVAP canister purge valve is OFF:
[a]: Unground “BLK” harness side terminal of EVAP canister purge valve.
EVAP canister purge valve is ON:
[b]: Ground “BLK” harness side terminal of EVAP canister purge valve.

s1.ptxt: Disconnect vacuum hose from intake manifold and purge hose from EVAP canister purge valve (1).
Connect special tool to vacuum hose (2) and set the tool in “VACUUM” mode.

attention3.ptxt: Before using special tool (vacuum pump gauge), read its Operator’s Manual to know how to use it.

s1.ptxt: Connect MAF sensor with IAT sensor-1 connector.
Check EVAP canister purge valve operation as follows.

s2.ptxt: Check that negative pressure of –60 kPa (–0.6 kgf/cm2, –8.7 psi, –0.6 bar) can be applied when EVAP canister purge valve is turned off [A].
Check that no negative pressure can be applied when EVAP canister purge valve is turned on [B].
